timeline_events.summary: Edward Snowden enlisted in the US Army Reserve as a special forces recruit but was discharged on 2004-09-28 without completing training or receiving awards.
Edward Snowden, an NSA whistleblower, had revelations first published in the Guardian revealing widespread data trawling by UK and US spy agencies.

Edward Snowden, an NSA contractor, worked with journalist Laura Poitras and others in a Hong Kong hotel room over eight days to publicly reveal the NSA's post-9/11 surveillance programs, as documented in the film Citizenfour.
Edward Snowden identified himself as the whistleblower who provided the Guardian with top-secret NSA documents leading to revelations about US surveillance on phone and internet communications.

The Guardian published the first revelations from top-secret material leaked by NSA contractor Edward Snowden, a court order requiring Verizon Business Services to hand over call records of all its customers.

Edward Snowden gave an interview in Hong Kong in which he said he was a patriot and explained his motivation for leaking classified NSA surveillance information, saying mass surveillance was "not something I'm willing to live under."
Edward Snowden provided documents to journalists Glenn Greenwald and Laura Poitras, leading to the Guardian publishing the first article revealing NSA phone records collection.

Edward Snowden publicly revealed his identity as the source of leaks of classified US National Security Agency surveillance documents, after leaving his NSA contractor job in Hawaii and traveling to Hong Kong.
Edward Snowden left his Hong Kong hotel and went into hiding.
The British government reportedly warned airlines not to allow NSA whistleblower Edward Snowden to fly to the UK because he is highly likely to be refused entry.
Edward Snowden flees to Hong Kong, where experts say he faces a precarious legal position but could buy time if he applies for asylum.
Edward Snowden is identified as the author of a cyber-leak revealing the US National Security Agency's Prism surveillance programme, prompting debate over whether he is a traitor or a whistleblower.

Legal experts say Hong Kong is unlikely to offer Edward Snowden permanent refuge, but he could buy time by filing an asylum request due to a March court ruling that requires the government to independently screen refugee cases.
Representative Peter King proclaimed Edward Snowden a "defector."
Edward Snowden is publicly revealed as the whistleblower responsible for leaking top-secret NSA surveillance documents.
Russia offers to consider an asylum request from US whistleblower Edward Snowden, though Snowden is not known to have made any asylum requests, including to Russia.
Legal experts say Edward Snowden could remain in Hong Kong for months or years if he chooses to fight any request for his return to the United States and if he asks for asylum.
Hong Kong activists plan a rally in support of Edward Snowden, calling on the US not to prosecute him and opposing extradition.
Edward Snowden tells the South China Morning Post he has no plans to leave Hong Kong and says he has evidence of US-led cyberespionage in Hong Kong and mainland China.
Files released by Edward Snowden to the Guardian reveal a vast NSA data collection operation gathering mobile phone metadata and online content with minimal oversight.
A demonstration took place outside the US consulate in Hong Kong in support of Edward Snowden, urging the city's government not to extradite him.
Edward Snowden denies speculation that he is a Chinese spy, stating he has had no contact with the Chinese government and only works with journalists.
The US government charged Edward Snowden with three felonies, including two under the Espionage Act.
WikiLeaks staff member Sarah Harrison, one of Julian Assange's closest advisors, is reported to be accompanying NSA whistleblower Edward Snowden as he seeks political asylum.
Edward Snowden leaves Hong Kong on a flight to Moscow after the US files espionage charges and requests his extradition.
Russia's foreign minister Sergei Lavrov said Edward Snowden never crossed the border into Russia, while the US continued to seek his extradition.
Russian President Vladimir Putin reveals that NSA whistleblower Edward Snowden is in a Moscow airport transit area and vows that Moscow will not extradite him to the US.
Ecuador says it could take months to decide whether to grant asylum to Edward Snowden, potentially confining him to a Russian airport transit area.
Article discusses Ecuador as a potential asylum refuge for Edward Snowden, noting no confirmed move or grant of asylum.
President Obama said the US will not engage in "wheeling and dealing" to persuade foreign governments to return Edward Snowden to the United States.
Edward Snowden applied for political asylum in Russia and 20 other countries through his WikiLeaks handler, Sarah Harrison.
Glenn Greenwald is to publish a book about Edward Snowden's exposure of mass US government surveillance, which will contain new revelations about NSA surveillance programs.

Ecuador's President Rafael Correa said Ecuador is not considering Edward Snowden's asylum request and never intended to facilitate his flight from Hong Kong, stating Snowden is Russia's responsibility and must reach Ecuadorean territory before any asylum request would be considered.
Edward Snowden accused President Obama of deception over extradition and asylum, saying the US revoked his passport and pressured other nations to deny his asylum requests.
UN Secretary General Ban Ki-moon says Edward Snowden misused his right to digital access, creating problems that outweigh the benefits of public disclosure.
Edward Snowden withdrew his request for political asylum from Russia after President Vladimir Putin said he would only be welcome if he stopped harming the United States.

Edward Snowden remains stalled at a Moscow airport while awaiting the apparently diminishing chance of asylum elsewhere, as the article argues he should leave Russia and be treated as a whistleblower rather than a spy.
Edward Snowden's requests for political asylum were rejected by multiple countries, including Brazil, India, Norway, and Poland, while he remained confined in Moscow's Sheremetyevo airport.
Edward Snowden has applied for asylum in 21 countries, with several rejecting his request and others yet to respond.
Oliver Stone defends Edward Snowden, calling him a "hero" for exposing the US's mass surveillance programme.
Bolivia offers asylum to Edward Snowden, following provisional asylum offers from Nicaragua and Venezuela.
A Russian official suggests Venezuela's asylum offer may be Edward Snowden's last chance to avoid extradition to the US.

The US Supreme Court is asked to suspend the blanket collection of US telephone records by the FBI under an emergency petition filed by the Electronic Privacy Information Center, following Edward Snowden's disclosure of secret NSA surveillance orders.

The Guardian reports that top-secret documents provided by Edward Snowden show Microsoft collaborated closely with the NSA to allow interception of users' communications, including helping circumvent its own encryption.
Edward Snowden remains stuck in Moscow's Sheremetyevo airport, seeking temporary asylum in Russia to allow him to file for asylum elsewhere while evading US extradition.
Edward Snowden invited human rights groups to meet him at a Moscow airport, claiming US officials are waging an unlawful campaign to prevent him from taking up asylum offers.
Edward Snowden applied for temporary asylum in Russia, telling immigration officials he fears for his life.
Guardian editors destroyed computer hard drives containing documents leaked by Edward Snowden under the supervision of GCHQ technicians.
Edward Snowden's lawyer says Snowden intends to remain in Russia long-term and is seeking temporary asylum, though his asylum status has not been resolved.

Edward Snowden's lawyer Anatoly Kucherena said he bought his client a copy of Crime and Punishment while Snowden was stuck in a Moscow transit lounge awaiting a decision on his application for temporary asylum.
US Attorney General Eric Holder tells Russia in a letter that the US will not seek the death penalty for Edward Snowden if he is extradited, in an attempt to prevent Moscow from granting him asylum.
Edward Snowden's father says the FBI asked him to fly to Moscow to encourage his son to return to the United States, and that he would prefer Edward remain in Russia.
Edward Snowden was granted asylum in Russia and left the Moscow airport where he had been stranded for more than a month.
Edward Snowden granted asylum in Russia.
Former NSA and CIA director Michael Hayden speculated that hackers and transparency groups might respond with cyber-terror attacks if the U.S. government apprehends Edward Snowden.
Russian senator Ruslan Gattarov began a campaign to raise funds for Edward Snowden, claiming Snowden is running out of money.
Russian migration authorities state that Edward Snowden is not in Moscow and has not registered his residence in the capital.

The Guardian editor-in-chief wrote that two GCHQ security experts visited the Guardian on 20 July and oversaw the destruction of hard drives containing copies of information provided by NSA whistleblower Edward Snowden.
The UK information commissioner announced that expert advisers were investigating the impact of Edward Snowden's disclosures concerning mass internet surveillance on the privacy of UK citizens.

A Fisa court judge ordered the government to review for declassification secret rulings about NSA surveillance, acknowledging that Edward Snowden's disclosures had triggered an important public debate.
Edward Snowden's Russian lawyer says Snowden is living under guard at a secret location in Russia but can travel freely without being recognized.
UK Information Commissioner Christopher Graham asks expert advisers to investigate the impact of Edward Snowden's disclosures on the privacy of UK citizens.

The head of the UK parliamentary intelligence and security committee, Sir Malcolm Rifkind, acknowledges that Edward Snowden has raised "real issues" about privacy safeguards while defending British intelligence agencies' spying techniques.
Guardian Faber acquires world rights to "The Snowden Files," a book by Luke Harding about Edward Snowden and the biggest leak in history, scheduled for publication in Spring 2014.
The first verified photograph of Edward Snowden in Russia appears, showing him meeting four former US government officials who presented him with an award for integrity in intelligence.
Edward Snowden was awarded the Sam Adams prize for integrity in intelligence.

The UK government conceded for the first time that Edward Snowden's revelations raise wider concerns about the balance between privacy and security, while the prime minister encouraged parliament to investigate the Guardian for publishing the material.
Edward Snowden said he left all leaked NSA documents behind when he flew from Hong Kong to Moscow and that there is no chance of them falling into the hands of Russian or Chinese authorities.

Edward Snowden says in an interview with the New York Times that he became a whistleblower because he had no faith in the US government's internal reporting mechanisms, which he believed would have buried his warnings forever.
Edward Snowden meets German Green politician Hans-Christian Ströbele in Moscow and indicates willingness to testify as a witness to the Bundestag about NSA surveillance.
The Guardian published a top-secret NSA document provided by Edward Snowden revealing the key role private companies play in NSA data collection.
Sarah Harrison, a WikiLeaks staffer who had been working with Edward Snowden in Moscow, arrived in Berlin after leaving Russia, saying she was advised it was not safe to return to the UK.
More than 50 German public figures call for Edward Snowden to be offered asylum in Germany, while Der Spiegel publishes a "manifesto for truth" written by Snowden.
The UK information commissioner expresses concern over the scale of NSA surveillance revealed by Edward Snowden, saying security cannot trump every other consideration.

A senior UN official warns that the UK government's response to mass surveillance revealed by Edward Snowden is damaging the UK's international reputation for investigative journalism and press freedom.
The EU executive threatens to freeze crucial data-sharing arrangements with the US because of the Edward Snowden revelations about mass NSA surveillance.
Index on Censorship criticizes the EU for failing to defend Edward Snowden as a whistleblower or issue a strong collective statement against mass surveillance.

Edward Snowden publishes an open letter to the Brazilian people, offering to assist Brazilian senators investigating suspected crimes against Brazilian citizens and stating he would rather be without a state than without a voice.
A top-secret Pentagon report assessing damage from Edward Snowden's leak of classified NSA documents concluded that the scope of compromised US intelligence knowledge is "staggering."
Edward Snowden first appeared on stage as the Snowbot telepresence robot to discuss internet freedom at a TED talk.
The Freedom of the Press Foundation announced that NSA whistleblower Edward Snowden will join its board of directors in February 2014.
Australia's foreign minister Julie Bishop brands Edward Snowden a traitor for leaking classified material, while welcoming US moves to review intelligence gathering.
Officials are planning to review the D-notice system in the wake of the Guardian's stories about mass surveillance based on leaks from Edward Snowden.
Guardian Faber is publishing "The Snowden Files: The Inside Story of the World's Most Wanted Man" by Luke Harding, the first book on Edward Snowden.
Edward Snowden reportedly used inexpensive web crawler software to scrape about 1.7 million classified NSA documents, according to intelligence officials investigating the leak.
Former CIA and NSA director Michael Hayden downplays speculation that the US might offer a plea bargain to Edward Snowden.

Guardian journalists win a special investigation prize at the Paul Foot award for their work on the investigation into files leaked by Edward Snowden revealing mass surveillance by British and US intelligence agencies.
Labour's shadow home secretary Yvette Cooper is preparing to propose substantial changes to oversight of British intelligence agencies in response to Edward Snowden's leaked files.
Edward Snowden, speaking via video link from Russia at the SXSW conference, said his NSA leaks had improved US national security and that he would do it again.
Edward Snowden spoke out at SXSW against former NSA Director Keith Alexander's renewed push for legislation to shut down media leaks.

Edward Snowden spoke at a keynote panel discussion at the SXSW technology and culture festival in Austin, Texas, focusing on the impact of NSA spying on the technology community and ways technology can protect against mass surveillance.

The US intelligence community attempts to rebrand itself via a Tumblr that publishes declassified surveillance documents, often omitting that releases followed transparency lawsuits, in the wake of Edward Snowden's disclosures.

Edward Snowden appeared via videolink from Russia at SXSW 2014, calling for internet users to adopt encryption and anonymous browsing technology and encouraging technology companies to make them more accessible.
Guardian editor Alan Rusbridger receives a European Press Prize special award for leading the paper's reporting on Edward Snowden's leaked NSA files.

NSA general counsel Rajesh De testified that US tech companies had full knowledge of the agency's data collection under Section 702, including the Prism program revealed through documents leaked by Edward Snowden.
Journalists Glenn Greenwald and Laura Poitras dedicated a George Polk Award for national security reporting to Edward Snowden, their source for the NSA surveillance revelations.
Edward Snowden issued a statement congratulating the Guardian and Washington Post on winning the 2014 Pulitzer Prize for Public Service for reporting on his NSA disclosures.

Edward Snowden defends his decision to question Vladimir Putin on mass surveillance during a live Russian television call-in, saying he aimed to hold Putin accountable rather than act as a propaganda tool.
Glenn Greenwald says his forthcoming book on Edward Snowden will contain new stories and revelations from the Snowden archive.
Edward Snowden questioned Vladimir Putin live on Russia Today about mass surveillance, and Putin denied that Russia has a mass interception system.

A Commons home affairs select committee report concludes that Edward Snowden's disclosures of mass surveillance are an "embarrassing indictment" of weak oversight of Britain's security and intelligence agencies and calls for radical reform.
A graphic biography of Edward Snowden, titled Beyond: Edward Snowden, is published by Bluewater Productions.

The NSA released an April 2013 email exchange to dispute Edward Snowden's claim that he raised concerns internally about its surveillance practices before going public, saying he was merely asking a legal question about training material.
Oliver Stone is set to direct a film adaptation of The Snowden Files, focusing on Edward Snowden's NSA whistleblowing, with shooting due to start before the end of 2014.

One year after the Guardian published the first stories based on documents provided by Edward Snowden, the article assesses how he changed the world and notes that key surveillance-reform questions remain unresolved.

Oliver Stone buys rights to a forthcoming novel based on Edward Snowden's life, written by Snowden's Russian lawyer Anatoly Kucherena, to use along with The Snowden Files as basis for a film screenplay.
Hillary Clinton discusses NSA whistleblower Edward Snowden during a full interview in the UK while promoting her memoir Hard Choices.
Edward Snowden condemns the UK's emergency surveillance bill, criticizing the speed of its passage, lack of public debate, and expanded intrusion powers.
Edward Snowden received a three-year residence permit in Russia, allowing him to remain and travel abroad for up to three months at a time.
Edward Snowden is given permission to stay in Russia.

Documents provided by Edward Snowden reveal that the New Zealand government implemented a secret mass surveillance program code-named "Speargun" throughout 2012 and 2013, and Snowden appeared via live stream at an Internet party event in Auckland to publicize the revelations.
Edward Snowden won a Guardian readers' poll for who should have received the 2014 Nobel peace prize, ahead of official winners Malala Yousafzai and Kailash Satyarthi.
Laura Poitras's documentary Citizenfour, about Edward Snowden and the NSA leaks, is scheduled to have its world premiere at the New York Film Festival.
Edward Snowden is scheduled to make his first UK public appearance via satellite link from Moscow at the Observer Ideas festival.
The Edward Snowden documentary Citizenfour opens in UK cinemas.
Shailene Woodley is in talks to play Edward Snowden's girlfriend, Lindsay Mills, in Oliver Stone's upcoming film about the NSA whistleblower.

A survey by the Canadian Centre for International Governance found that 60% of respondents globally had heard of Edward Snowden, but only 39% of those had taken additional steps to protect their online privacy as a result.

A study found that while 60% of internet users had heard of NSA whistleblower Edward Snowden, only 39% of those had taken additional steps to protect their online privacy, though security expert Bruce Schneier estimated that 706 million people worldwide had changed their online behavior because of the NSA and GCHQ surveillance revelations.

Edward Snowden received the Right Livelihood award in the Swedish parliament via video from Moscow for his revelations of state surveillance, with the award left uncollected in hope he could one day accept it in person.
The Council of Europe’s human rights commissioner said Edward Snowden’s disclosures showed secret, massive and indiscriminate surveillance that cannot be justified by the fight against terrorism.
A private US citizen sues the makers of the documentary Citizenfour, alleging they profited from Edward Snowden's theft and misuse of leaked government documents.
Laura Poitras's film Citizenfour, about exiled whistleblower Edward Snowden, was nominated for the best documentary Oscar.
Oliver Stone's film about Edward Snowden completes casting, with Zachary Quinto, Tom Wilkinson, and Melissa Leo set to play journalists and filmmaker involved in reporting Snowden's NSA leaks.
A UK court ruled that the secrecy surrounding a GCHQ mass surveillance program exposed by Edward Snowden was illegal, vindicating his whistleblowing.
Laura Poitras discusses her documentary Citizenfour, Edward Snowden, and whistleblowers ahead of its Australian release.
The documentary Citizenfour, about Edward Snowden's NSA revelations, won the Oscar for best documentary.
Edward Snowden, Glenn Greenwald, and Laura Poitras took questions from Reddit users during an AMA.

Edward Snowden's Russian lawyer said Snowden wants to return home and that lawyers are working to resolve the issue, while US justice department officials said he would have to face criminal charges if he returned.
Photos released from the set of Oliver Stone's biopic Snowden show Joseph Gordon-Levitt as Edward Snowden in military uniform.
The Wikimedia Foundation, Amnesty International and civil rights groups sued the NSA and the US Department of Justice over the mass surveillance programme uncovered by whistleblower Edward Snowden.

The UK Parliament's intelligence and security committee releases a report stating new spying legislation is needed following Edward Snowden's revelations about Western intelligence agencies' activities.

A US court of appeals rules that the NSA's bulk phone surveillance program, revealed by Edward Snowden, exceeded what the Patriot Act allowed, and the article argues Snowden should be granted amnesty.
The National Security Agency lost key powers, primarily the bulk collection of phone data, a development described as a huge victory for whistleblower Edward Snowden.

Edward Snowden said in a New York Times piece that the balance of power has shifted as people defy government surveillance, citing the end of mass surveillance of private telephone calls under the US Patriot Act as a landmark victory.
The US Senate passes the USA Freedom Act, ending the NSA's bulk collection of phone records, a legislative change attributed to Edward Snowden's revelations.
Reports claim Russia and China accessed Edward Snowden's leaked files, forcing British agents to be withdrawn from operations, though the claims rely on anonymous sources and are disputed.
The Sunday Times quietly deleted an allegation that David Miranda met Edward Snowden in Moscow before being detained at Heathrow, and the Daily Mail removed the same claim pending inquiries.
The FBI requested that Denmark, Norway, Sweden, and Finland arrest and extradite Edward Snowden if he traveled to those countries, according to newly released documents.
The Obama administration rejected a petition to pardon Edward Snowden, reiterating that he should face criminal charges for leaking classified information.

Actor Joseph Gordon-Levitt reveals he secretly met Edward Snowden in Russia for four hours to prepare for Oliver Stone's film Snowden, saying he believes Snowden acted because he thought it was right.
Edward Snowden is to attend via video link a New York meeting launching a draft international "Snowden Treaty" aimed at strengthening privacy laws and protecting whistleblowers.
Edward Snowden joined Twitter under the verified handle @Snowden, quickly attracting over 70,000 followers.
Edward Snowden said the US justice department has not contacted him to discuss a plea deal that would allow him to return from exile in Russia.

The European Parliament voted 285-281 to call on EU member states to prevent Edward Snowden's extradition to the US and grant him protection, a resolution Snowden praised as "extraordinary" and a "game-changer."

The UK government published draft surveillance legislation in response to Edward Snowden's disclosures, consolidating bulk data collection and adding more intrusive powers, while the US had passed the USA Freedom Act restricting bulk data collection.
Edward Snowden made a virtual appearance at the Consumer Electronics Show via a Suitable Technologies Beam robot, speaking in an onstage interview with Peter Diamandis.
The Danish government revealed that a US government jet was stationed at Copenhagen airport in June 2013, likely to extradite Edward Snowden if he had arrived in Scandinavia.
Edward Snowden said in a video interview at the RightsCon technology conference in San Francisco that he is not an unhappy ending and hopes to encourage more future whistleblowers.
Jean-Michel Jarre collaborates with Edward Snowden on a techno track titled Exit, featuring Snowden speaking, after the Guardian put them in touch.
Edward Snowden condemned Australian law enforcement for collecting a Guardian journalist's communications records without a warrant, saying "the scandal is what the law allows."
The trailer for Oliver Stone's fact-based thriller Snowden, starring Joseph Gordon-Levitt as Edward Snowden, is released.
Edward Snowden's lawyers vow to make a new push for a presidential pardon from Barack Obama, though Snowden concedes a pardon is unlikely before Obama leaves office.
Edward Snowden is set to appear via video screen alongside Daniel Radcliffe in the off-Broadway play Privacy in New York City.

Edward Snowden appeared via satellite at San Diego Comic-Con for a Q&A with director Oliver Stone about the film "Snowden," saying he lives "a surprisingly free life" in Russia but still cannot come home.
Oliver Stone discusses his film about Edward Snowden, reflecting on its production and his meetings with Snowden.
Oliver Stone’s biopic Snowden, starring Joseph Gordon-Levitt as Edward Snowden, is set to premiere at the Toronto International Film Festival in September.
Supporters of Edward Snowden are raising funds to help refugees who hid him in Hong Kong in 2013, after lawyer Robert Tibbo revealed Snowden had stayed with them and sent each $1,000.
Oliver Stone's film "Snowden," about NSA whistleblower Edward Snowden, is set to screen at the Toronto film festival.
Oliver Stone's film "Snowden," about NSA whistleblower Edward Snowden, received its world premiere at the Toronto film festival.
Edward Snowden made a moral case for a presidential pardon, arguing that his 2013 surveillance disclosures were necessary and benefited the public.

Edward Snowden set out the case for Barack Obama granting him a pardon before the US president leaves office, arguing that the disclosure of surveillance by US and British intelligence agencies was morally right and had left citizens better off.
Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov praised Oliver Stone's biopic "Snowden" as "top quality" and "nearly a documentary," urging people to see it as it opens in Russia and the US.
The Washington Post editorial board published an editorial against pardoning Edward Snowden, prompting renewed debate over a pardon.
Former NSA deputy director Chris Inglis criticizes Oliver Stone's biopic of Edward Snowden as a "preposterous" and gross mischaracterization of the NSA's purposes and Snowden's role.

Edward Snowden reacted on Twitter to the arrest of NSA contractor Harold Thomas Martin III, who worked for the same company as Snowden, questioning whether the FBI had secretly arrested the person behind reports that the NSA sat on huge flaws in US products.
Messages calling for a pardon for Edward Snowden were projected onto the exterior wall of the Newseum in Washington by the Pardon Snowden campaign without the museum's knowledge or approval.

The House intelligence committee released declassified portions of a report claiming Edward Snowden has had and continues to have contact with Russian intelligence services, a claim Snowden and his lawyer rejected.

Edward Snowden cited an unverified NBC report that Russia may return him to the US as a “gift” to Donald Trump as evidence that he never cooperated with Russian intelligence, while his lawyer said Team Snowden had received no such signals.
Edward Snowden disclosed the extent of the global eavesdropping operation run by the NSA, GCHQ, and their partners.
Edward Snowden talks NSA and internet surveillance at SXSW.
Cartoonist Ted Rall published a graphic biography titled Snowden about NSA whistleblower Edward Snowden.
Experts are divided over the extradition of NSA whistleblower Edward Snowden.

Edward Snowden remained stuck in Moscow’s Sheremetyevo International Airport after efforts to transit to a South American country failed, and he sought temporary asylum in Russia with help from lawyer Anatoly Kucherena.
Edward Snowden comments that the rush to pass a British surveillance law is extraordinary.
Hong Kong silent over Edward Snowden extradition.

facts.text: On 2013-06-09, Edward Snowden publicly revealed his identity as the source of leaks of classified US National Security Agency surveillance documents, after leaving his NSA contractor job in Hawaii and traveling to Hong Kong.
On 2013-06-21, the US government charged Edward Snowden with three felonies, including two under the Espionage Act; he left Hong Kong for Moscow on 2013-06-23.
On 2013-06-26, Ecuador said it could take months to decide whether to grant asylum to Edward Snowden, potentially confining him to a Russian airport transit area.
On 2013-08-01, Edward Snowden was granted asylum in Russia and left the Moscow airport where he had been stranded for more than a month.
On 2014-01-14, the Freedom of the Press Foundation announced that NSA whistleblower Edward Snowden will join its board of directors in February 2014.
On 2014-03-10, Edward Snowden, speaking via video link from Russia at the SXSW conference, said his NSA leaks had improved US national security and that he would do it again.
On 2014-04-14, Edward Snowden issued a statement congratulating the Guardian and Washington Post on winning the 2014 Pulitzer Prize for Public Service for reporting on his NSA disclosures.

On 2016-07-21, Edward Snowden appeared via satellite at San Diego Comic-Con for a Q&A with director Oliver Stone about the film "Snowden," saying he lives "a surprisingly free life" in Russia but still cannot come home.

event-e0d7003fa73668b9.summary: Edward Snowden invited human rights groups to meet him at a Moscow airport, claiming US officials are waging an unlawful campaign to prevent him from taking up asylum offers.

event-9ac3ab0f753787d6.summary: Edward Snowden applied for temporary asylum in Russia, telling immigration officials he fears for his life.

event-633f77cf24a1a4bf.summary: Guardian editors destroyed computer hard drives containing documents leaked by Edward Snowden under the supervision of GCHQ technicians.

event-6056af8c2f69876e.summary: Edward Snowden's lawyer says Snowden intends to remain in Russia long-term and is seeking temporary asylum, though his asylum status has not been resolved.

event-5e17fae70c3d2a58.summary: Edward Snowden's lawyer Anatoly Kucherena said he bought his client a copy of Crime and Punishment while Snowden was stuck in a Moscow transit lounge awaiting a decision on his application for temporary asylum.

event-7cd4a79087d6d60d.summary: US Attorney General Eric Holder tells Russia in a letter that the US will not seek the death penalty for Edward Snowden if he is extradited, in an attempt to prevent Moscow from granting him asylum.

event-809618af6b9916d2.summary: Edward Snowden's father says the FBI asked him to fly to Moscow to encourage his son to return to the United States, and that he would prefer Edward remain in Russia.

event-cc14bc920f1f2045.summary: Edward Snowden was granted asylum in Russia and left the Moscow airport where he had been stranded for more than a month.

event-f3f4e62d7cd86c13.summary: Edward Snowden granted asylum in Russia.

event-7bb4698124e4dfbc.summary: Former NSA and CIA director Michael Hayden speculated that hackers and transparency groups might respond with cyber-terror attacks if the U.S. government apprehends Edward Snowden.

event-02d0deaa19e86de4.summary: Russian senator Ruslan Gattarov began a campaign to raise funds for Edward Snowden, claiming Snowden is running out of money.

event-ace49a9f361b6559.summary: Russian migration authorities state that Edward Snowden is not in Moscow and has not registered his residence in the capital.

event-c8a338d605f8aff6.summary: The Guardian editor-in-chief wrote that two GCHQ security experts visited the Guardian on 20 July and oversaw the destruction of hard drives containing copies of information provided by NSA whistleblower Edward Snowden.

event-0d9e458954bd67be.summary: The UK information commissioner announced that expert advisers were investigating the impact of Edward Snowden's disclosures concerning mass internet surveillance on the privacy of UK citizens.

event-8120fbd32f8f3e0e.summary: A Fisa court judge ordered the government to review for declassification secret rulings about NSA surveillance, acknowledging that Edward Snowden's disclosures had triggered an important public debate.

event-facc3634b17b4573.summary: Edward Snowden's Russian lawyer says Snowden is living under guard at a secret location in Russia but can travel freely without being recognized.

event-a2871d2ebffdad1f.summary: UK Information Commissioner Christopher Graham asks expert advisers to investigate the impact of Edward Snowden's disclosures on the privacy of UK citizens.

event-9ffee1768bbafc9a.summary: The head of the UK parliamentary intelligence and security committee, Sir Malcolm Rifkind, acknowledges that Edward Snowden has raised "real issues" about privacy safeguards while defending British intelligence agencies' spying techniques.

event-c3ebfb9587cf16e2.summary: Guardian Faber acquires world rights to "The Snowden Files," a book by Luke Harding about Edward Snowden and the biggest leak in history, scheduled for publication in Spring 2014.

event-c54630f2a0e148ea.summary: The first verified photograph of Edward Snowden in Russia appears, showing him meeting four former US government officials who presented him with an award for integrity in intelligence.

event-9696bda14e3cea76.summary: Edward Snowden was awarded the Sam Adams prize for integrity in intelligence.

event-5152655e2dea14ae.summary: The UK government conceded for the first time that Edward Snowden's revelations raise wider concerns about the balance between privacy and security, while the prime minister encouraged parliament to investigate the Guardian for publishing the material.

event-26339d437ef67bb5.summary: Edward Snowden said he left all leaked NSA documents behind when he flew from Hong Kong to Moscow and that there is no chance of them falling into the hands of Russian or Chinese authorities.

event-ec773e947f60a626.summary: Edward Snowden says in an interview with the New York Times that he became a whistleblower because he had no faith in the US government's internal reporting mechanisms, which he believed would have buried his warnings forever.

event-5314e0946376a799.summary: Edward Snowden meets German Green politician Hans-Christian Ströbele in Moscow and indicates willingness to testify as a witness to the Bundestag about NSA surveillance.

event-547875c9c9f49895.summary: The Guardian published a top-secret NSA document provided by Edward Snowden revealing the key role private companies play in NSA data collection.

event-f702e22527c72451.summary: Sarah Harrison, a WikiLeaks staffer who had been working with Edward Snowden in Moscow, arrived in Berlin after leaving Russia, saying she was advised it was not safe to return to the UK.

event-44ec50248fafb6ed.summary: More than 50 German public figures call for Edward Snowden to be offered asylum in Germany, while Der Spiegel publishes a "manifesto for truth" written by Snowden.

event-7e896daaa5c6d4fa.summary: The UK information commissioner expresses concern over the scale of NSA surveillance revealed by Edward Snowden, saying security cannot trump every other consideration.

event-c7fe6d3d1f585554.summary: A senior UN official warns that the UK government's response to mass surveillance revealed by Edward Snowden is damaging the UK's international reputation for investigative journalism and press freedom.

event-4a963c7c85faabc2.summary: The EU executive threatens to freeze crucial data-sharing arrangements with the US because of the Edward Snowden revelations about mass NSA surveillance.

event-f1351ba59d14e3cf.summary: Index on Censorship criticizes the EU for failing to defend Edward Snowden as a whistleblower or issue a strong collective statement against mass surveillance.

event-a7f1066aeaf10055.summary: Edward Snowden publishes an open letter to the Brazilian people, offering to assist Brazilian senators investigating suspected crimes against Brazilian citizens and stating he would rather be without a state than without a voice.

event-dfc60b917cc72e0a.summary: A top-secret Pentagon report assessing damage from Edward Snowden's leak of classified NSA documents concluded that the scope of compromised US intelligence knowledge is "staggering."

event-952a9311ecd861a3.summary: Edward Snowden first appeared on stage as the Snowbot telepresence robot to discuss internet freedom at a TED talk.

event-0246ce5f7c40b857.summary: The Freedom of the Press Foundation announced that NSA whistleblower Edward Snowden will join its board of directors in February 2014.

event-dc6aa999626a7d49.summary: Australia's foreign minister Julie Bishop brands Edward Snowden a traitor for leaking classified material, while welcoming US moves to review intelligence gathering.

event-27292bb26002fcfd.summary: Officials are planning to review the D-notice system in the wake of the Guardian's stories about mass surveillance based on leaks from Edward Snowden.

event-2fed83addd3939e2.summary: Guardian Faber is publishing "The Snowden Files: The Inside Story of the World's Most Wanted Man" by Luke Harding, the first book on Edward Snowden.

event-8c92605adb901f47.summary: Edward Snowden reportedly used inexpensive web crawler software to scrape about 1.7 million classified NSA documents, according to intelligence officials investigating the leak.

event-c006cda2327212ba.summary: Former CIA and NSA director Michael Hayden downplays speculation that the US might offer a plea bargain to Edward Snowden.

event-56a6181c70e19808.summary: Guardian journalists win a special investigation prize at the Paul Foot award for their work on the investigation into files leaked by Edward Snowden revealing mass surveillance by British and US intelligence agencies.

event-e8ccc5469d4faa4c.summary: Labour's shadow home secretary Yvette Cooper is preparing to propose substantial changes to oversight of British intelligence agencies in response to Edward Snowden's leaked files.

event-12b30ae2f55e9e04.summary: Edward Snowden, speaking via video link from Russia at the SXSW conference, said his NSA leaks had improved US national security and that he would do it again.

event-3d27570000990c1a.summary: Edward Snowden spoke out at SXSW against former NSA Director Keith Alexander's renewed push for legislation to shut down media leaks.

event-e8b3c843bfa7bc5d.summary: Edward Snowden spoke at a keynote panel discussion at the SXSW technology and culture festival in Austin, Texas, focusing on the impact of NSA spying on the technology community and ways technology can protect against mass surveillance.

event-8882c5bd18935ea8.summary: The US intelligence community attempts to rebrand itself via a Tumblr that publishes declassified surveillance documents, often omitting that releases followed transparency lawsuits, in the wake of Edward Snowden's disclosures.

event-aa19635546af6780.summary: Edward Snowden appeared via videolink from Russia at SXSW 2014, calling for internet users to adopt encryption and anonymous browsing technology and encouraging technology companies to make them more accessible.

event-15119e3d0ab1fe27.summary: Guardian editor Alan Rusbridger receives a European Press Prize special award for leading the paper's reporting on Edward Snowden's leaked NSA files.

event-f4a0616f17b701ff.summary: NSA general counsel Rajesh De testified that US tech companies had full knowledge of the agency's data collection under Section 702, including the Prism program revealed through documents leaked by Edward Snowden.

event-2346092154191993.summary: Journalists Glenn Greenwald and Laura Poitras dedicated a George Polk Award for national security reporting to Edward Snowden, their source for the NSA surveillance revelations.

event-dc28541cf5a4144d.summary: Edward Snowden issued a statement congratulating the Guardian and Washington Post on winning the 2014 Pulitzer Prize for Public Service for reporting on his NSA disclosures.

event-274a7b7eaabb27b2.summary: Edward Snowden defends his decision to question Vladimir Putin on mass surveillance during a live Russian television call-in, saying he aimed to hold Putin accountable rather than act as a propaganda tool.

event-0f837d7f0bbace1b.summary: Glenn Greenwald says his forthcoming book on Edward Snowden will contain new stories and revelations from the Snowden archive.

event-4e48695199e04679.summary: Edward Snowden questioned Vladimir Putin live on Russia Today about mass surveillance, and Putin denied that Russia has a mass interception system.

event-5c24c6f6237925d9.summary: A Commons home affairs select committee report concludes that Edward Snowden's disclosures of mass surveillance are an "embarrassing indictment" of weak oversight of Britain's security and intelligence agencies and calls for radical reform.

event-6e7cdb1f355e3b1e.summary: A graphic biography of Edward Snowden, titled Beyond: Edward Snowden, is published by Bluewater Productions.

event-8dd230589dcd2e08.summary: The NSA released an April 2013 email exchange to dispute Edward Snowden's claim that he raised concerns internally about its surveillance practices before going public, saying he was merely asking a legal question about training material.

event-f5bef45a66d3ff00.summary: Oliver Stone is set to direct a film adaptation of The Snowden Files, focusing on Edward Snowden's NSA whistleblowing, with shooting due to start before the end of 2014.

event-961264becf436ae3.summary: One year after the Guardian published the first stories based on documents provided by Edward Snowden, the article assesses how he changed the world and notes that key surveillance-reform questions remain unresolved.

event-f2bd127a714d8d71.summary: Oliver Stone buys rights to a forthcoming novel based on Edward Snowden's life, written by Snowden's Russian lawyer Anatoly Kucherena, to use along with The Snowden Files as basis for a film screenplay.

event-04827f8bbb486495.summary: Hillary Clinton discusses NSA whistleblower Edward Snowden during a full interview in the UK while promoting her memoir Hard Choices.

event-d5fcac4e25ad9fde.summary: Edward Snowden condemns the UK's emergency surveillance bill, criticizing the speed of its passage, lack of public debate, and expanded intrusion powers.

event-3ab4a02ebf89b603.summary: Edward Snowden received a three-year residence permit in Russia, allowing him to remain and travel abroad for up to three months at a time.

event-692d9ae96ccddc5f.summary: Edward Snowden is given permission to stay in Russia.

event-9a38eef11134b986.summary: Documents provided by Edward Snowden reveal that the New Zealand government implemented a secret mass surveillance program code-named "Speargun" throughout 2012 and 2013, and Snowden appeared via live stream at an Internet party event in Auckland to publicize the revelations.

event-3fc5f70e0400320a.summary: Edward Snowden won a Guardian readers' poll for who should have received the 2014 Nobel peace prize, ahead of official winners Malala Yousafzai and Kailash Satyarthi.

event-70637f7a6cbd222d.summary: Laura Poitras's documentary Citizenfour, about Edward Snowden and the NSA leaks, is scheduled to have its world premiere at the New York Film Festival.

event-af701ff8c470afed.summary: Edward Snowden is scheduled to make his first UK public appearance via satellite link from Moscow at the Observer Ideas festival.

event-c30493e2475be116.summary: The Edward Snowden documentary Citizenfour opens in UK cinemas.

event-5e6764f13c1e3a75.summary: Shailene Woodley is in talks to play Edward Snowden's girlfriend, Lindsay Mills, in Oliver Stone's upcoming film about the NSA whistleblower.

event-5e57abaa9b0281aa.summary: A survey by the Canadian Centre for International Governance found that 60% of respondents globally had heard of Edward Snowden, but only 39% of those had taken additional steps to protect their online privacy as a result.

event-634d37623ed2a607.summary: A study found that while 60% of internet users had heard of NSA whistleblower Edward Snowden, only 39% of those had taken additional steps to protect their online privacy, though security expert Bruce Schneier estimated that 706 million people worldwide had changed their online behavior because of the NSA and GCHQ surveillance revelations.

event-5aba40a36fe9740c.summary: Edward Snowden received the Right Livelihood award in the Swedish parliament via video from Moscow for his revelations of state surveillance, with the award left uncollected in hope he could one day accept it in person.

event-5f751ea440c395b7.summary: The Council of Europe’s human rights commissioner said Edward Snowden’s disclosures showed secret, massive and indiscriminate surveillance that cannot be justified by the fight against terrorism.

event-91af64c03be082c3.summary: A private US citizen sues the makers of the documentary Citizenfour, alleging they profited from Edward Snowden's theft and misuse of leaked government documents.

event-02a30ce42d3a8d73.summary: Laura Poitras's film Citizenfour, about exiled whistleblower Edward Snowden, was nominated for the best documentary Oscar.

event-9195681640363bdd.summary: Oliver Stone's film about Edward Snowden completes casting, with Zachary Quinto, Tom Wilkinson, and Melissa Leo set to play journalists and filmmaker involved in reporting Snowden's NSA leaks.

event-d1e6e0a51cbf38ba.summary: A UK court ruled that the secrecy surrounding a GCHQ mass surveillance program exposed by Edward Snowden was illegal, vindicating his whistleblowing.

event-549e6b91c5cca0e7.summary: Laura Poitras discusses her documentary Citizenfour, Edward Snowden, and whistleblowers ahead of its Australian release.

event-5341d497daa3d42c.summary: The documentary Citizenfour, about Edward Snowden's NSA revelations, won the Oscar for best documentary.

event-6affd9bbce38ab39.summary: Edward Snowden, Glenn Greenwald, and Laura Poitras took questions from Reddit users during an AMA.

event-dab164fac807c39e.summary: Edward Snowden's Russian lawyer said Snowden wants to return home and that lawyers are working to resolve the issue, while US justice department officials said he would have to face criminal charges if he returned.

event-6170f6d6343c49b2.summary: Photos released from the set of Oliver Stone's biopic Snowden show Joseph Gordon-Levitt as Edward Snowden in military uniform.

event-fe5cbbd213dc0dc7.summary: The Wikimedia Foundation, Amnesty International and civil rights groups sued the NSA and the US Department of Justice over the mass surveillance programme uncovered by whistleblower Edward Snowden.

event-58ad601b2b07ef80.summary: The UK Parliament's intelligence and security committee releases a report stating new spying legislation is needed following Edward Snowden's revelations about Western intelligence agencies' activities.

event-1d493abacb0503f7.summary: A US court of appeals rules that the NSA's bulk phone surveillance program, revealed by Edward Snowden, exceeded what the Patriot Act allowed, and the article argues Snowden should be granted amnesty.

event-a69b0cf986b9ad20.summary: The National Security Agency lost key powers, primarily the bulk collection of phone data, a development described as a huge victory for whistleblower Edward Snowden.

event-152c2896c81757f3.summary: Edward Snowden said in a New York Times piece that the balance of power has shifted as people defy government surveillance, citing the end of mass surveillance of private telephone calls under the US Patriot Act as a landmark victory.

event-fd0b010ef400cd32.summary: The US Senate passes the USA Freedom Act, ending the NSA's bulk collection of phone records, a legislative change attributed to Edward Snowden's revelations.

event-399b1ef2793de36b.summary: Reports claim Russia and China accessed Edward Snowden's leaked files, forcing British agents to be withdrawn from operations, though the claims rely on anonymous sources and are disputed.

event-60c4f68ec3331d77.summary: The Sunday Times quietly deleted an allegation that David Miranda met Edward Snowden in Moscow before being detained at Heathrow, and the Daily Mail removed the same claim pending inquiries.

event-3a0c53cadc575dc6.summary: The FBI requested that Denmark, Norway, Sweden, and Finland arrest and extradite Edward Snowden if he traveled to those countries, according to newly released documents.

event-0ce5a42be1b9ca8a.summary: The Obama administration rejected a petition to pardon Edward Snowden, reiterating that he should face criminal charges for leaking classified information.

event-bb0465e09bc090bf.summary: Actor Joseph Gordon-Levitt reveals he secretly met Edward Snowden in Russia for four hours to prepare for Oliver Stone's film Snowden, saying he believes Snowden acted because he thought it was right.

event-d4c1acb50bb8cd69.summary: Edward Snowden is to attend via video link a New York meeting launching a draft international "Snowden Treaty" aimed at strengthening privacy laws and protecting whistleblowers.

event-402de1144aed43f9.summary: Edward Snowden joined Twitter under the verified handle @Snowden, quickly attracting over 70,000 followers.

event-78652c4bcd8c0b48.summary: Edward Snowden said the US justice department has not contacted him to discuss a plea deal that would allow him to return from exile in Russia.

event-39c22b7c84388a1f.summary: The European Parliament voted 285-281 to call on EU member states to prevent Edward Snowden's extradition to the US and grant him protection, a resolution Snowden praised as "extraordinary" and a "game-changer."

event-9f83f7f442e2700d.summary: The UK government published draft surveillance legislation in response to Edward Snowden's disclosures, consolidating bulk data collection and adding more intrusive powers, while the US had passed the USA Freedom Act restricting bulk data collection.

event-73aa78d8e3fdd8e3.summary: Edward Snowden made a virtual appearance at the Consumer Electronics Show via a Suitable Technologies Beam robot, speaking in an onstage interview with Peter Diamandis.

event-6e568656ebf6e09b.summary: The Danish government revealed that a US government jet was stationed at Copenhagen airport in June 2013, likely to extradite Edward Snowden if he had arrived in Scandinavia.

event-01c5bb893d5a4271.summary: Edward Snowden said in a video interview at the RightsCon technology conference in San Francisco that he is not an unhappy ending and hopes to encourage more future whistleblowers.

event-1485086da773e8cf.summary: Jean-Michel Jarre collaborates with Edward Snowden on a techno track titled Exit, featuring Snowden speaking, after the Guardian put them in touch.

event-2e2122f72bbf40a7.summary: Edward Snowden condemned Australian law enforcement for collecting a Guardian journalist's communications records without a warrant, saying "the scandal is what the law allows."

event-b984b951e9ab17aa.summary: The trailer for Oliver Stone's fact-based thriller Snowden, starring Joseph Gordon-Levitt as Edward Snowden, is released.

event-d5bef7ee05dbd559.summary: Edward Snowden's lawyers vow to make a new push for a presidential pardon from Barack Obama, though Snowden concedes a pardon is unlikely before Obama leaves office.

event-a72d3c2ff04e9397.summary: Edward Snowden is set to appear via video screen alongside Daniel Radcliffe in the off-Broadway play Privacy in New York City.

event-648e14bd88a4098c.summary: Edward Snowden appeared via satellite at San Diego Comic-Con for a Q&A with director Oliver Stone about the film "Snowden," saying he lives "a surprisingly free life" in Russia but still cannot come home.

event-4ac31c3ead098269.summary: Oliver Stone discusses his film about Edward Snowden, reflecting on its production and his meetings with Snowden.

event-15af3f2e19eb5272.summary: Oliver Stone’s biopic Snowden, starring Joseph Gordon-Levitt as Edward Snowden, is set to premiere at the Toronto International Film Festival in September.

event-bbef23013138b4c3.summary: Supporters of Edward Snowden are raising funds to help refugees who hid him in Hong Kong in 2013, after lawyer Robert Tibbo revealed Snowden had stayed with them and sent each $1,000.

event-a14713298617839c.summary: Oliver Stone's film "Snowden," about NSA whistleblower Edward Snowden, is set to screen at the Toronto film festival.

event-83f6d07b46764fca.summary: Oliver Stone's film "Snowden," about NSA whistleblower Edward Snowden, received its world premiere at the Toronto film festival.

event-422ac1c35603708a.summary: Edward Snowden made a moral case for a presidential pardon, arguing that his 2013 surveillance disclosures were necessary and benefited the public.

event-25422417e1ebd781.summary: Edward Snowden set out the case for Barack Obama granting him a pardon before the US president leaves office, arguing that the disclosure of surveillance by US and British intelligence agencies was morally right and had left citizens better off.

event-92403b62a8fdedab.summary: Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov praised Oliver Stone's biopic "Snowden" as "top quality" and "nearly a documentary," urging people to see it as it opens in Russia and the US.

event-621ffe9860d2c28a.summary: The Washington Post editorial board published an editorial against pardoning Edward Snowden, prompting renewed debate over a pardon.

event-6145cd93519fddd1.summary: Former NSA deputy director Chris Inglis criticizes Oliver Stone's biopic of Edward Snowden as a "preposterous" and gross mischaracterization of the NSA's purposes and Snowden's role.

event-c38b5961c2c4cd6c.summary: Edward Snowden reacted on Twitter to the arrest of NSA contractor Harold Thomas Martin III, who worked for the same company as Snowden, questioning whether the FBI had secretly arrested the person behind reports that the NSA sat on huge flaws in US products.

event-a8ad2a155ee1a6ef.summary: Messages calling for a pardon for Edward Snowden were projected onto the exterior wall of the Newseum in Washington by the Pardon Snowden campaign without the museum's knowledge or approval.

event-a551f1d707a81749.summary: The House intelligence committee released declassified portions of a report claiming Edward Snowden has had and continues to have contact with Russian intelligence services, a claim Snowden and his lawyer rejected.

event-3cb3c9933474a89f.summary: Edward Snowden cited an unverified NBC report that Russia may return him to the US as a “gift” to Donald Trump as evidence that he never cooperated with Russian intelligence, while his lawyer said Team Snowden had received no such signals.

event-2dad9b4c9187056d.summary: Edward Snowden disclosed the extent of the global eavesdropping operation run by the NSA, GCHQ, and their partners.

event-3f9b30656661c7d3.summary: Edward Snowden talks NSA and internet surveillance at SXSW.

event-6464dd67e562ece2.summary: Cartoonist Ted Rall published a graphic biography titled Snowden about NSA whistleblower Edward Snowden.

event-a901ffea90d02b84.summary: Experts are divided over the extradition of NSA whistleblower Edward Snowden.

event-dd4b45c503937994.summary: Edward Snowden remained stuck in Moscow’s Sheremetyevo International Airport after efforts to transit to a South American country failed, and he sought temporary asylum in Russia with help from lawyer Anatoly Kucherena.

event-e41a5010597636d5.summary: Edward Snowden comments that the rush to pass a British surveillance law is extraordinary.

event-fe9c2eeb5105971c.summary: Hong Kong silent over Edward Snowden extradition.

events.summary: Edward Snowden is publicly revealed as the whistleblower responsible for leaking top-secret NSA surveillance documents.
Edward Snowden reportedly used inexpensive web crawler software to scrape about 1.7 million classified NSA documents, according to intelligence officials investigating the leak.
Former NSA deputy director Chris Inglis criticizes Oliver Stone's biopic of Edward Snowden as a "preposterous" and gross mischaracterization of the NSA's purposes and Snowden's role.
Oliver Stone is set to direct a film adaptation of The Snowden Files, focusing on Edward Snowden's NSA whistleblowing, with shooting due to start before the end of 2014.
President George W. Bush appoints former Presidents George H.W. Bush and Bill Clinton to launch a joint appeal for emergency donations to victims of the Indian Ocean tsunami.
Former NSA and CIA director Michael Hayden speculated that hackers and transparency groups might respond with cyber-terror attacks if the U.S. government apprehends Edward Snowden.

Edward Snowden remains stalled at a Moscow airport while awaiting the apparently diminishing chance of asylum elsewhere, as the article argues he should leave Russia and be treated as a whistleblower rather than a spy.
Edward Snowden joined Twitter under the verified handle @Snowden, quickly attracting over 70,000 followers.

Edward Snowden reacted on Twitter to the arrest of NSA contractor Harold Thomas Martin III, who worked for the same company as Snowden, questioning whether the FBI had secretly arrested the person behind reports that the NSA sat on huge flaws in US products.
A top-secret Pentagon report assessing damage from Edward Snowden's leak of classified NSA documents concluded that the scope of compromised US intelligence knowledge is "staggering."
Former CIA and NSA director Michael Hayden downplays speculation that the US might offer a plea bargain to Edward Snowden.
Jean-Michel Jarre collaborates with Edward Snowden on a techno track titled Exit, featuring Snowden speaking, after the Guardian put them in touch.
Edward Snowden identified himself as the whistleblower who provided the Guardian with top-secret NSA documents leading to revelations about US surveillance on phone and internet communications.
Edward Snowden provided documents to journalists Glenn Greenwald and Laura Poitras, leading to the Guardian publishing the first article revealing NSA phone records collection.
Edward Snowden is to attend via video link a New York meeting launching a draft international "Snowden Treaty" aimed at strengthening privacy laws and protecting whistleblowers.
The National Security Agency lost key powers, primarily the bulk collection of phone data, a development described as a huge victory for whistleblower Edward Snowden.

A Fisa court judge ordered the government to review for declassification secret rulings about NSA surveillance, acknowledging that Edward Snowden's disclosures had triggered an important public debate.
The UK information commissioner announced that expert advisers were investigating the impact of Edward Snowden's disclosures concerning mass internet surveillance on the privacy of UK citizens.
President Obama said the US will not engage in "wheeling and dealing" to persuade foreign governments to return Edward Snowden to the United States.

The Guardian published the first revelations from top-secret material leaked by NSA contractor Edward Snowden, a court order requiring Verizon Business Services to hand over call records of all its customers.

The European Parliament voted 285-281 to call on EU member states to prevent Edward Snowden's extradition to the US and grant him protection, a resolution Snowden praised as "extraordinary" and a "game-changer."
Australia's foreign minister Julie Bishop brands Edward Snowden a traitor for leaking classified material, while welcoming US moves to review intelligence gathering.

A survey by the Canadian Centre for International Governance found that 60% of respondents globally had heard of Edward Snowden, but only 39% of those had taken additional steps to protect their online privacy as a result.
Edward Snowden was granted asylum in Russia and left the Moscow airport where he had been stranded for more than a month.

facts.text: On 2004-05-07, Edward Snowden enlisted in the US Army Reserve as a special forces recruit but was discharged on 2004-09-28 without completing training or receiving awards.
On 2013-06-05, the Guardian published the first Snowden leak: a secret court order requiring Verizon Business Services to hand over call records of all its customers.
On 2013-06-09, Edward Snowden publicly revealed his identity as the source of leaks of classified NSA surveillance documents, after leaving his contractor job in Hawaii for Hong Kong.
On 2013-06-23, Edward Snowden left Hong Kong on a flight to Moscow after the US filed espionage charges and requested his extradition.
On 2013-08-01, Edward Snowden was granted asylum in Russia and left the Moscow airport where he had been stranded for more than a month.
On 2014-10-10, Laura Poitras's documentary Citizenfour, about Edward Snowden and the NSA leaks, was scheduled to have its world premiere at the New York Film Festival.
On 2015-05-07, a US court of appeals ruled that the NSA's bulk phone surveillance program revealed by Snowden exceeded what the Patriot Act allowed.
On 2015-06-06, the US Senate passed the USA Freedom Act, ending the NSA's bulk collection of phone records, a change attributed to Snowden's revelations.

events.summary: Edward Snowden publicly revealed his identity as the source of leaks of classified US National Security Agency surveillance documents, after leaving his NSA contractor job in Hawaii and traveling to Hong Kong.
Edward Snowden leaves Hong Kong on a flight to Moscow after the US files espionage charges and requests his extradition.
Edward Snowden provided documents to journalists Glenn Greenwald and Laura Poitras, leading to the Guardian publishing the first article revealing NSA phone records collection.

Edward Snowden, an NSA contractor, worked with journalist Laura Poitras and others in a Hong Kong hotel room over eight days to publicly reveal the NSA's post-9/11 surveillance programs, as documented in the film Citizenfour.
Laura Poitras's documentary Citizenfour, about Edward Snowden and the NSA leaks, is scheduled to have its world premiere at the New York Film Festival.
Edward Snowden left his Hong Kong hotel and went into hiding.
Edward Snowden is to attend via video link a New York meeting launching a draft international "Snowden Treaty" aimed at strengthening privacy laws and protecting whistleblowers.
Edward Snowden left Hong Kong for Moscow after the US requested his arrest, despite previously saying he would stay and fight in court.
Laura Poitras discusses her documentary Citizenfour, Edward Snowden, and whistleblowers ahead of its Australian release.
Supporters of Edward Snowden are raising funds to help refugees who hid him in Hong Kong in 2013, after lawyer Robert Tibbo revealed Snowden had stayed with them and sent each $1,000.
Sarah Harrison, a WikiLeaks staffer who had been working with Edward Snowden in Moscow, arrived in Berlin after leaving Russia, saying she was advised it was not safe to return to the UK.
Edward Snowden was allowed to leave Hong Kong and flew to Moscow despite a US request for his detention and extradition on espionage charges.
Edward Snowden received a three-year residence permit in Russia, allowing him to remain and travel abroad for up to three months at a time.
Edward Snowden was granted asylum in Russia and left the Moscow airport where he had been stranded for more than a month.
Edward Snowden applied for temporary asylum in Russia, telling immigration officials he fears for his life.
Russia grants Edward Snowden temporary asylum, drawing a mixed reception among Russian human rights activists.
Edward Snowden renewed his request for political asylum in Russia during a meeting with human rights activists at Moscow's Sheremetyevo airport, his first public appearance since fleeing Hong Kong.
Edward Snowden applied for political asylum in Russia and 20 other countries through his WikiLeaks handler, Sarah Harrison.
Edward Snowden withdrew his request for political asylum from Russia after President Vladimir Putin said he would only be welcome if he stopped harming the United States.
Russia offers to consider an asylum request from US whistleblower Edward Snowden, though Snowden is not known to have made any asylum requests, including to Russia.

Edward Snowden's lawyer says Snowden intends to remain in Russia long-term and is seeking temporary asylum, though his asylum status has not been resolved.

Edward Snowden cited an unverified NBC report that Russia may return him to the US as a “gift” to Donald Trump as evidence that he never cooperated with Russian intelligence, while his lawyer said Team Snowden had received no such signals.
A private US citizen sues the makers of the documentary Citizenfour, alleging they profited from Edward Snowden's theft and misuse of leaked government documents.

One year after the Guardian published the first stories based on documents provided by Edward Snowden, the article assesses how he changed the world and notes that key surveillance-reform questions remain unresolved.

The UK government conceded for the first time that Edward Snowden's revelations raise wider concerns about the balance between privacy and security, while the prime minister encouraged parliament to investigate the Guardian for publishing the material.
Glenn Greenwald is to publish a book about Edward Snowden's exposure of mass US government surveillance, which will contain new revelations about NSA surveillance programs.
Edward Snowden identified himself as the whistleblower who provided the Guardian with top-secret NSA documents leading to revelations about US surveillance on phone and internet communications.
Guardian Faber acquires world rights to "The Snowden Files," a book by Luke Harding about Edward Snowden and the biggest leak in history, scheduled for publication in Spring 2014.

The US Supreme Court is asked to suspend the blanket collection of US telephone records by the FBI under an emergency petition filed by the Electronic Privacy Information Center, following Edward Snowden's disclosure of secret NSA surveillance orders.
The US government charged Edward Snowden with three felonies, including two under the Espionage Act.

The US intelligence community attempts to rebrand itself via a Tumblr that publishes declassified surveillance documents, often omitting that releases followed transparency lawsuits, in the wake of Edward Snowden's disclosures.
Officials are planning to review the D-notice system in the wake of the Guardian's stories about mass surveillance based on leaks from Edward Snowden.
UN Secretary General Ban Ki-moon says Edward Snowden misused his right to digital access, creating problems that outweigh the benefits of public disclosure.

events.summary: Edward Snowden flees to Hong Kong, where experts say he faces a precarious legal position but could buy time if he applies for asylum.
Legal experts say Edward Snowden could remain in Hong Kong for months or years if he chooses to fight any request for his return to the United States and if he asks for asylum.

The US charged NSA whistleblower Edward Snowden with theft of government property, unauthorised communication of national defence information, and wilful communication of classified communications intelligence to an unauthorised person.

Edward Snowden chooses Hong Kong as a haven to leak intelligence documents and unmask himself as a whistleblower, a decision described as a high-stakes gamble due to Hong Kong's extradition treaty with the US.
Edward Snowden tells the South China Morning Post he has no plans to leave Hong Kong and says he has evidence of US-led cyberespionage in Hong Kong and mainland China.

Legal experts say Hong Kong is unlikely to offer Edward Snowden permanent refuge, but he could buy time by filing an asylum request due to a March court ruling that requires the government to independently screen refugee cases.

On 2013-06-21, the US government charged Edward Snowden with three felonies, including two under the Espionage Act; he left Hong Kong for Moscow on 2013-06-23.
On 2013-07-01, Edward Snowden accused President Obama of deception over extradition and asylum, saying the US revoked his passport and pressured other nations to deny his asylum requests.
On 2013-08-01, Edward Snowden was granted asylum in Russia and left the Moscow airport where he had been stranded for more than a month.
On 2013-10-31, Edward Snowden met German Green politician Hans-Christian Ströbele in Moscow and indicated willingness to testify as a witness to the Bundestag about NSA surveillance.
On 2015-06-06, the US Senate passed the USA Freedom Act, ending the NSA's bulk collection of phone records, a change attributed to Snowden's revelations.

A US court of appeals rules that the NSA's bulk phone surveillance program, revealed by Edward Snowden, exceeded what the Patriot Act allowed, and the article argues Snowden should be granted amnesty.

The Guardian identifies Edward Snowden as the source who leaked classified NSA surveillance information.
Edward Snowden joined Twitter under the verified handle @Snowden, quickly attracting over 70,000 followers.
The Guardian published a top-secret NSA document provided by Edward Snowden revealing the key role private companies play in NSA data collection.

Edward Snowden provided documents to journalists Glenn Greenwald and Laura Poitras, leading to the Guardian publishing the first article revealing NSA phone records collection.

The US charged NSA whistleblower Edward Snowden with theft of government property, unauthorised communication of national defence information, and wilful communication of classified communications intelligence to an unauthorised person.
Legal experts say Edward Snowden could remain in Hong Kong for months or years if he chooses to fight any request for his return to the United States and if he asks for asylum.
Edward Snowden tells the South China Morning Post he has no plans to leave Hong Kong and says he has evidence of US-led cyberespionage in Hong Kong and mainland China.

Edward Snowden chooses Hong Kong as a haven to leak intelligence documents and unmask himself as a whistleblower, a decision described as a high-stakes gamble due to Hong Kong's extradition treaty with the US.
Hong Kong activists plan a rally in support of Edward Snowden, calling on the US not to prosecute him and opposing extradition.

Edward Snowden was granted asylum in Russia and left the Moscow airport where he had been stranded for more than a month.

Russia grants Edward Snowden temporary asylum, drawing a mixed reception among Russian human rights activists.
US Attorney General Eric Holder tells Russia in a letter that the US will not seek the death penalty for Edward Snowden if he is extradited, in an attempt to prevent Moscow from granting him asylum.
Edward Snowden was granted temporary asylum in Russia and left the Moscow airport where he had stayed for over a month.

Edward Snowden's Russian lawyer says Snowden is living under guard at a secret location in Russia but can travel freely without being recognized.

events.summary: Edward Snowden spoke at a keynote panel discussion at the SXSW technology and culture festival in Austin, Texas, focusing on the impact of NSA spying on the technology community and ways technology can protect against mass surveillance.
Edward Snowden talks NSA and internet surveillance at SXSW.
Edward Snowden, speaking via video link from Russia at the SXSW conference, said his NSA leaks had improved US national security and that he would do it again.

The Guardian published the first revelations from top-secret material leaked by NSA contractor Edward Snowden, a court order requiring Verizon Business Services to hand over call records of all its customers.
Edward Snowden identified himself as the whistleblower who provided the Guardian with top-secret NSA documents leading to revelations about US surveillance on phone and internet communications.

A study found that while 60% of internet users had heard of NSA whistleblower Edward Snowden, only 39% of those had taken additional steps to protect their online privacy, though security expert Bruce Schneier estimated that 706 million people worldwide had changed their online behavior because of the NSA and GCHQ surveillance revelations.

NSA general counsel Rajesh De testified that US tech companies had full knowledge of the agency's data collection under Section 702, including the Prism program revealed through documents leaked by Edward Snowden.

One year after the Guardian published the first stories based on documents provided by Edward Snowden, the article assesses how he changed the world and notes that key surveillance-reform questions remain unresolved.

The NSA released an April 2013 email exchange to dispute Edward Snowden's claim that he raised concerns internally about its surveillance practices before going public, saying he was merely asking a legal question about training material.
Edward Snowden spoke out at SXSW against former NSA Director Keith Alexander's renewed push for legislation to shut down media leaks.
Edward Snowden revealed he was the source of leaked details on the NSA's Prism surveillance programme.
Edward Snowden identifies himself as the source of leaks of top-secret NSA documents to the Guardian.
Edward Snowden received a three-year residence permit in Russia, allowing him to remain and travel abroad for up to three months at a time.
Edward Snowden was granted asylum in Russia and left the Moscow airport where he had been stranded for more than a month.
Edward Snowden applied for temporary asylum in Russia, telling immigration officials he fears for his life.
Russia grants Edward Snowden temporary asylum, drawing a mixed reception among Russian human rights activists.
Edward Snowden applied for political asylum in Russia and 20 other countries through his WikiLeaks handler, Sarah Harrison.
Edward Snowden renewed his request for political asylum in Russia during a meeting with human rights activists at Moscow's Sheremetyevo airport, his first public appearance since fleeing Hong Kong.
Russia offers to consider an asylum request from US whistleblower Edward Snowden, though Snowden is not known to have made any asylum requests, including to Russia.
Edward Snowden's lawyer says Snowden intends to remain in Russia long-term and is seeking temporary asylum, though his asylum status has not been resolved.
Edward Snowden withdrew his request for political asylum from Russia after President Vladimir Putin said he would only be welcome if he stopped harming the United States.
Edward Snowden was granted temporary asylum in Russia and left the Moscow airport where he had stayed for over a month.
Edward Snowden granted asylum in Russia.
Edward Snowden was granted asylum in Russia for one year and left Moscow's Sheremetyevo airport for an undisclosed location.
A private US citizen sues the makers of the documentary Citizenfour, alleging they profited from Edward Snowden's theft and misuse of leaked government documents.
Guardian Faber acquires world rights to "The Snowden Files," a book by Luke Harding about Edward Snowden and the biggest leak in history, scheduled for publication in Spring 2014.
Glenn Greenwald is to publish a book about Edward Snowden's exposure of mass US government surveillance, which will contain new revelations about NSA surveillance programs.

Glenn Greenwald says his forthcoming book on Edward Snowden will contain new stories and revelations from the Snowden archive.

The UK government conceded for the first time that Edward Snowden's revelations raise wider concerns about the balance between privacy and security, while the prime minister encouraged parliament to investigate the Guardian for publishing the material.
The Wikimedia Foundation, Amnesty International and civil rights groups sued the NSA and the US Department of Justice over the mass surveillance programme uncovered by whistleblower Edward Snowden.
A graphic biography of Edward Snowden, titled Beyond: Edward Snowden, is published by Bluewater Productions.
Edward Snowden leaves Hong Kong on a flight to Moscow after the US files espionage charges and requests his extradition.

The US Supreme Court is asked to suspend the blanket collection of US telephone records by the FBI under an emergency petition filed by the Electronic Privacy Information Center, following Edward Snowden's disclosure of secret NSA surveillance orders.
